Shawn Jewkes Today as we were calibrating the MD & XR in L3 issues were brought to our attention about MD checks on the TG's causing the line to stop. 
Our calibration rep identified that the alarm is because the pieces jump over the sensor when being rejected so the machine thinks there were no ejected pieces. 
Working with maintenance and (Jakob? German tech.), there are a few things that could be done:
1. Lower the cover so that pieces can't jump over the height of the sensor. 
2. Fabricate a guard so that pieces hit that and fall through the sensor. 
3. Lower/play with the air pressure so that pieces don't blow so high. 
 
Maybe you're aware of this already? 
The German tech seems to believe we are losing a total of about 5% production time due to these stops from QA CCP checks. 
 
Just wanted to get it in front of you, if not already...
Thank you for bringing it up. I wasn't aware. We'll create an action in the CI tracker and investigate options

Issue: when the caps get stuck the white tamping block is taking a long time to activate and release the jam.

The timing was delayed due to the CAP CHUTE HIGH EYE being adjusted to see the edge of the metal: it was on all the time. This Eye and the Cap Chute Low eye can start the Tamping Cycle. Without the First EYE working it will wait for the Low eye and give the appearance that it is waiting too long to start.
